title: Security event logging scope and content
status_rationale: SOC2-012 and SOC2-002 direct monitoring scope and event content; GOV-AUTH-012 requires tamper-evident logging of authority decisions; none implemented.
target_answer: Unbound emits a versioned catalog of security events covering authentication, MFA changes, authorization denials, privilege and role changes, reads and exports of sensitive data, configuration and integration changes, administrative and break-glass actions, database-level activity outside the application and AI agent actions. Each record carries actor, authority used, action, resource, decision, result, occurredAt and recordedAt, correlation id and policy version. Automated tests prove every catalog event is emitted.
current_practice: Not established; no production system. Aegis provides fault capture with redaction for .NET applications, which is operational fault handling, not security event logging.
intended_practice: Implement the event catalog in Unbound's governed APIs and persistence layer.
customer_statement: Unbound's security logging is designed but not implemented; we can share the designed event scope.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Log integrity and tamper evidence
status_rationale: SOC2-006, UNB-DATA-008, UNB-DATA-012 and UNB-IMM-007 require append-only history, tamper-evident digests and independent verification; mechanism unbenchmarked and Strata capabilities unverified.
target_answer: Authoritative audit history is append-only below the application API; update and delete are denied to all application, administrator and agent roles; logs are stored in a separate trust domain; hash chains or signed checkpoints are verified daily and after any restore; customers and auditors can verify exported trails independently; access to logs is itself logged.
intended_practice: Benchmark the integrity mechanism and verify Strata and PostgreSQL permission model.
customer_statement: Tamper-evident, append-only audit history is a design requirement for Unbound; it is not yet implemented or verified.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

challenge.customer_intent: Audit trails that an insider or attacker cannot quietly alter.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Fraud or intrusion concealed by log modification.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional answers cite access restrictions and WORM storage; these protect storage but rarely prove completeness, and administrators of the logging platform can often still delete or omit records.
challenge.legally_required: Not for Echelon directly. SEC Rule 17a-4 imposes non-rewriteable or audit-trail recordkeeping on broker-dealers for required records, which can flow to a vendor that holds them.
challenge.historical_convention: Restricted access plus immutable storage tier.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Append-only history below the application API (UNB-DATA-008), with corrections as linked new records, removes the update path entirely within scope.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Database permissions that deny update and delete on authoritative history to every application and administrative role.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Hash chain or signed checkpoint verification detecting omission, alteration, duplication and reordering (UNB-DATA-012), verifiable by the customer.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structural append-only history plus customer-verifiable integrity proofs anchored outside Echelon's trust domain.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by design; the customer or auditor can recompute proofs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Strata or PostgreSQL configuration permitting superuser rewrite without detection; checkpoints anchored in the same trust domain.
challenge.alternative_risks: Append-only storage conflicts with lawful deletion of personal data unless redaction or crypto-shredding is designed in (SOC2-032).
supporting_arguments: Unbound requirements already direct this design.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely, once explained; it exceeds the conventional answer.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Mechanism is unbenchmarked; Strata capabilities are unverified.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

history.change: BL-021: set institutional_acceptance to unknown (prior 'likely' was unsourced agent judgment, kept in supporting_arguments) and added an unvalidated-acceptance note to opposing_arguments (OBJ-VRM-019, OBJ-SKEPTIC-014).

title: Log retention and privacy-aware logging
status_rationale: SOC2-003 prohibits secrets and unnecessary sensitive data in logs; SOC2-023 forbids inventing universal retention periods without auditor and counsel input; REQ-X-036 sets seven-year minimum retention for financial documents but not security logs.
target_answer: Security logs are retained at least 12 months online-searchable and longer in archive per a counsel-approved schedule by log class, with tenant-specific extension and legal hold; typed log schemas exclude secrets and restrict personal data at emission; personal data in append-only logs is handled by field-level redaction or key destruction so lawful deletion is possible.
intended_practice: Set retention schedule with counsel and auditor (SOC2-023).
customer_statement: Log retention periods have not yet been set; they will be defined with counsel and auditors.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: What retention period will apply to security logs, and does any customer regulation (for example Rule 17a-4 or Rule 204-2) require longer retention of records held in Unbound?

title: SIEM, alerting, after-hours coverage and response
status_rationale: No monitoring platform, on-call arrangement or MDR provider is identified. Vigila, which the Standard proposed for runtime monitoring, is a task organizer, not a monitoring system.
target_answer: Security events are centralized in an analysis platform with correlation across API, agent, persistence and cloud control plane sources; high-severity alerts page an on-call responder 24x7 with a 15-minute acknowledgment target (conditional on a staffed rotation or a contracted MDR provider); pre-approved automated protective actions (account disablement, agent credential revocation, tenant payment hold under the sponsor-adopted hold policy) execute on high-confidence signals; detection and response times are measured and reported.
current_practice: Unknown; no evidence located. Current position (2026-11-25): Echelon has one principal, the managing member, and no staff, on-call rotation or contracted support provider, so this commitment cannot be met today.
intended_practice: Select a monitoring platform and staffing model before production.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet selected a security monitoring platform or established after-hours coverage.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Will Echelon use an MDR provider, and would it be a subprocessor with access to customer data?
Who provides after-hours coverage given current organization size?

challenge.customer_intent: Someone will notice and act on an attack at any hour.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Overnight or weekend attack proceeds undetected until business hours.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: A staffed 24x7 SOC is effective but costly; small vendors claiming 24x7 coverage often mean an unstaffed alert email.
challenge.legally_required: No law reviewed requires a vendor to staff 24x7 monitoring.
challenge.contractually_required: Sometimes asked by banks; usually as a question rather than a contractual term.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Fail-closed holds on consequential operations (CNV-PLT-007) and automatic protective actions limit damage when no human is awake.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Pre-approved automated containment on high-confidence signals (freeze payments for a tenant, disable account, revoke agent credential).
challenge.stronger_alternative: Automated protective actions plus paging on-call with documented response time, optionally an MDR provider for infrastructure telemetry.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through alert and action timing metrics and tabletop results.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Single on-call person; automated actions with high false positive rates disrupting sponsor operations.
challenge.alternative_risks: Automated holds could disrupt time-sensitive grants; must follow sponsor-adopted hold policy.
supporting_arguments: Automated containment acts in seconds; humans in minutes to hours.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain: banks may still expect named 24x7 coverage.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Key-person dependency in a very small organization.
MDR adds a subprocessor with data access.

title: Detection engineering
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-ECO-016 references detection coverage and seeded-control test pass rate as counter-metrics; TVR-SEC-008 requires matching of IdP admin actions and custody movements; no detection catalog exists.
target_answer: Detections are maintained as versioned code mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and to domain abuse cases (payee change followed by disbursement request, unusual grant velocity, bulk export, cross-tenant probing, account takeover indicators, agent scope violations); each detection is tested with seeded events on change and monthly; false positive rates are tracked.
intended_practice: Build the detection catalog alongside the event catalog.
customer_statement: Detection engineering is planned; not yet operating.

title: Customer administrator audit trail
status_rationale: SOC2-009 requires auditor-ready evidence export with chain of custody; UNB-XIN-IAM-005 requires notifying tenant administrators of break-glass within 1 hour; no customer audit UI exists.
target_answer: Customer administrators can view, search, export and stream (near real time, in a documented JSON schema) all audit events for their tenant, including actions by Echelon personnel, support and break-glass sessions; tenant-visible logs are retained for the contract term plus an agreed period and are exportable at termination; integrity proofs let the customer verify completeness independently; events are tenant-scoped so no tenant can see another's events.
intended_practice: Implement with the event catalog and tenant isolation model.
customer_statement: A customer-visible audit trail is part of Unbound's design; it is not yet implemented.

title: Missing heartbeat and log pipeline failure detection
status_rationale: SOC2-027 requires that a missing expected log or heartbeat create a monitored control exception, and the continuous control monitoring architecture specifies a missing-evidence algorithm and treats monitoring failure as a degraded-assurance incident; specified, not implemented.
target_answer: An independent expectation engine schedules expected evidence by control, source and period; missing or late sources raise preserved deficiencies within one hour; monitoring failure is a degraded-assurance incident; consequential grant and payment actions follow sponsor-approved fail-closed or manual-continuity policies while safety-critical monitoring is down; zero activity requires validated zero-activity evidence.
intended_practice: Implement per the continuous control monitoring architecture.
customer_statement: Detection of missing logs and heartbeats is specified for Unbound; not implemented.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

challenge.continuous_evidence: Evidence completeness ratio with raw denominators.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Computed assurance from expected evidence, as specified in the Unbound continuous control monitoring architecture.

title: AI agent activity logging and scope monitoring
status_rationale: For repository engineering work, Praxis records agent provenance (actor kind, provider, model, runtime, reason) in execution records, as seen in this repository's AGENTS.md front matter; this is tooling evidence, not a runtime control for a production service. SOC2-017 requires runtime agents to be attributable, bounded, monitored and interruptible; not implemented for Unbound.
target_answer: Every AI agent action in engineering and operations is attributable to a distinct agent identity, model and version, authorizing human or policy, and task; tool invocations and results are logged with classification-based redaction of prompts and outputs; out-of-scope actions are denied, logged and alerted, and agents can be interrupted with a kill switch.
current_practice: Praxis records agent provenance for repository changes in Echelon repositories. No runtime agent activity logging exists for Unbound.
intended_practice: Extend to Unbound runtime agents per SOC2-017.
provable: Praxis execution and provenance records in Echelon repositories (first-party, not independently verified).
customer_statement: For engineering work in its repositories, Echelon records which AI agent made a change and why; runtime agent activity logging for Unbound is planned, not implemented.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Prompt and output logging can capture sensitive data; redaction depends on correct classification.

title: Time synchronization
status_rationale: The Unbound evidence envelope requires occurredAt and recordedAt; no infrastructure exists to synchronize.
target_answer: All components synchronize to the hosting provider's authoritative time service; offsets are monitored and alert beyond 100 ms; records use UTC with millisecond precision and carry both occurredAt and recordedAt.
customer_statement: Time synchronization is planned with infrastructure selection.

title: Privileged, break-glass and pipeline monitoring
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-005 specifies sealed break-glass credentials, two-person activation, 4-hour expiry, security owner paging and tenant notification within 1 hour; CNV-PLT-010 requires two approvers and signed builds for control-relevant modules; not implemented.
target_answer: Break-glass and privileged production access are recorded at session level, page the security owner, notify affected tenant administrators within 1 hour and are reviewed after each use; changes to CI workflows, deploy credentials and signing keys are alerted and reviewed.

title: Threat intelligence sharing and use
status_rationale: No threat intelligence sharing membership or feed is in use; no detection program exists (ANS-MON-004 is unknown).
target_answer: Echelon receives sector threat intelligence (for example through FS-ISAC membership, a vendor feed or CISA advisories), records how each relevant item changed detections, dependency decisions or customer guidance, and shares indicators from its own incidents with customers and sharing partners where permitted.
intended_practice: Choose a feed proportionate to size (CISA and vendor advisories first; sector membership when eligible and affordable).
customer_statement: Echelon does not participate in a threat intelligence sharing organization today. It plans to consume sector and government advisories and to record how they change its detections.
